library(readr)
library(car)
AVONETdataset<- read_csv("AVONET Supplementary dataset 1.csv")
View(AVONETdataset)
str(AVONETdataset)
names(AVONETdataset)
summary(AVONETdataset)
AVONETdataset$Trophic.Niche<-as.factor(AVONETdataset$Trophic.Niche)
AVONETtrimmed<-AVONETdataset[,c("Beak.Length_Culmen","Beak.Length_Nares","Beak.Width","Beak.Depth","Tarsus.Length","Wing.Length","Kipps.Distance","Secondary1","Hand-Wing.Index","Tail.Length","Mass","Trophic.Niche")]
str(AVONETtrimmed)
summary(AVONETtrimmed)
##Assignment 1: Pick any dataset you have used before that has at least five numericpredictor variables, and at least one categorical predictor variable. With this dataset, do the following:
##Check whether your data are categorical, continuous, or ordinal. 
#My data is a combination of categorical, continuous, and ordinal
##Check the correlational structure of your predictor variables.
#Pearson's corr matrix
AVONETNUM<-AVONETtrimmed[,1:11]
AVONETCORR<-cor(AVONETNUM,use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
AVONETCORR
#The strongest correlations are Beak.Length_Culmen and Beak.Length_Nares at 0.9709664, Beak.Depth and Beak.Width at 0.9062487, Wing.Length and Secondary1 at 0.9267326, Beak.Length_Culmen and Beak.Width at 0.7442026, Beak.Length_Culmen and Beak.Depth at 0.7141237, Wing.Length and Kipps.Distance at 0.8807724, Tarsus.Length and Secondary1 at 0.80105408, Secondary1 and Tail.Length at 0.78148416, Tarsus.Length and Wing.Length at 0.75820227.
#Check if your data are linear.
pairs(AVONETNUM, 
      panel = function(x,y){
        points(x,y, cex=0.4,pch=18,col="springgreen")
        lines(lowess(x,y),col= "black", lwd=2)})
#The results are not all linear, I utilized a lowess smoothing curve to visualize. Combination of positive and nonlinear results.
##Check whether your dataset has any data missing.
colSums(is.na(AVONETtrimmed))
colMeans(is.na(AVONETtrimmed))*100
#Trophic niche has 0.09% missing, all my other values are 0
##Assignment 2: Using the dataset from Assignment 1, perform a principal components analysis.
#Use the prcomp() function in R, and make sure to center and scale as appropriate.
PCAanalysis<-prcomp(AVONETNUM,center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
summary(PCAanalysis)
#Broken stick
broken_stick<-function(P){
  sequence<- 1:P
  divided<- 1/sequence
  seq_sums<-sapply(sequence,FUN = function(k){
    subset<- divided[k:P]
    subset_sum<-sum(subset)
    i<- subset_sum/P
    return(i)
  })
  return(seq_sums)
}
broken_stick(11)
#for 11 variables
#Keep in mind you may need to adjust the dataset to ensure it follows the PCA assumptions
#Choose a cutoff for retained PCs
#Plot, pairwise, all retained PCs, color coding (or changing the PCH) by one of your categorical predictor variables.
#Retain only PC1, has 60.15% total variance and 27.45% broken stick, other PC are not variable. I cannot do a pairwiseplot due to the other PC values not being viable.  
#Explain the rotation and importance of your retained PCs.
PCAanalysis$rotation[,1]
#PC1 explained 60.15% of the total variance. All of the output values were negative for PC1, with several contributing the most out of all 11 morphological variables. Wing.Length is -0.3640333, Secondary1 is -0.3521020, Beak.Width is -0.3348063, Beak..Length_Culmen is -0.3343681  and Beak.Depth is -0.3271846 were the largest rotation values. 

PC1<-PCAanalysis$x[,1]
PC1
##Assignment 3: Using the dataset from Assignment 1, perform a non-parametric multidimensional scaling analysis.
#Use the vegan package in R
library(vegan)
library(permute)
#Missing values removal
AVONETclean<-AVONETtrimmed[!is.na(AVONETtrimmed$Trophic.Niche),]
#scale
set.seed(123)
#Had to shrink down species sample because R kept crashing
AVONETsubsample<-AVONETclean[
  sample(nrow(AVONETclean),300),]
AVONETcleanNPM<-scale(AVONETsubsample[,1:11])
NPM<-metaMDS(AVONETcleanNPM,distance = "euclidean", k=2,trymax = 50, maxit=500,autotransform = FALSE,trace = 1)
#I read that adjusting maxit and trymax values can lead to better stress values
#Keep in mind you may need to adjust the dataset to ensure it follows the NMDS assumptions.
#Plot the first two NMDS variables and explain any patterns you see in your dataset, color coding (or changing the PCH) by one of your categorical predictor variables
scoresNPM<-scores(NPM, display = "sites")
AVONETsubsample$Trophic.Niche<-droplevels(AVONETsubsample$Trophic.Niche)
colorsforNPM<-as.numeric(AVONETsubsample$Trophic.Niche)
plot(scoresNPM,cex=0.8,col=colorsforNPM,pch=19,xlab = "NMDS1",ylab = "NMDS2",main = "AVONET Bird Morphological Measurements NMDs")
legend("bottomleft",legend = levels(AVONETsubsample$Trophic.Niche),col=seq_along(levels(AVONETsubsample$Trophic.Niche)),pch=19,cex=0.4,ncol = 3,bty = "n")
#Discuss what results you see.
#NMDS analyses gave an output of 0.03856 for stress value which is significant in showing the differences between the 300 sampled bird species. There is a heavy overlap between different trophic niche categories (Trophic.Niche), forming no distinct clusters 
##Assignment 4: Using the dataset from Assignment 1, perform a linear discriminant analysis or quadratic discriminant analysis.
#I choose LDA as a better fit for my data
#Use the MASS and caret packages in R.
library(MASS)
library(caret)
LDAAVONET<-AVONETsubsample
LDAAVONET$Trophic.Niche<-as.factor(LDAAVONET$Trophic.Niche)
LDA<-lda(Trophic.Niche~.,data = LDAAVONET)
LDA
predictingLDA<-predict(LDA)
plot(predictingLDA$x[,1],predictingLDA$x[,2],col=as.numeric(LDAAVONET$Trophic.Niche),pch=19,cex=0.8,xlab = "LD1",ylab = "LD2",main = "AVONET Bird Morphological Measurements LDA")
legend("bottomright",legend = levels(LDAAVONET$Trophic.Niche),col=seq_along(levels(LDAAVONET$Trophic.Niche)),pch=19,cex=0.4,ncol = 3,bty = "n")
#Keep in mind you may need to adjust the dataset to ensure it follows the LDA/QDA assumptions.
#Plot the first two LDA/QDA variables and explain any patterns you see in your dataset, color coding (or changing the PCH) by one of your categorical predictor variables.
#Substantial overlap within frugivores, invertivores, granivores and aquatic predators. Nectarivores display the most separation. The samples for each group were not even, with herbivorous birds only making up 6 total samples (aquatic and terrestrial herbivores).
#For both plots R kept crashing whenever I tried to move the legend, had to greatly trim the dataset to even run the plots without R crashing
